audience: Engineers continuing from the DFlash marginal-distribution example.
prerequisites: DFlash predicts per-position marginals with shared conditioning fixed.
The target, not the draft score, determines emitted tokens.
objective: Follow a seven-prefix alternative tree into a flat ancestry mask and a target walk ending with the unmatched but emitted runs.
scope: All nine beats of the compact DDTree episode, including repaired rounded-product and final-ribbon construction. Source checks do not certify visual fidelity.
assumptions: Expected matched depth is explicitly under factorized draft Q, a proxy rather than a target acceptance guarantee.
Budget excludes anchor well. Flat order is root followed by best-first insertions, not BFS; position IDs remain depth-based.
Binary visibility includes root, ancestors and self. Positions add a common context offset to depth.
The matched a and model are followed by emitted runs; the anchor is new output even though absent from the proposed tree.
unknowns: No bound audiovisual review, event expectations or learner responses are supplied. The repaired scene constructs approximation-aware equations and replaces the next actual ribbon slot with runs, but rendered fidelity still needs review.

claims.statement: The high-mass prefix objective maximizes a draft-Q matched-depth surrogate under a finite non-root node budget.

evidence.support: Target expectation is infeasible at construction time; Q replaces it. The prefix sum follows from the matched-depth objective under Q.

claims.statement: Depth-derived positions and ancestry visibility preserve distinct branches in a flat target input.

evidence.support: A child's visibility is inherited from its parent plus self; positions are node depths plus start.

claims.statement: At a-model the missing target token runs stops reuse but is still emitted as the next anchor.

evidence.support: The returned next_token is written immediately after accepted tokens; absence from child_maps ends the cached walk, not token validity.
The toy target decisions are a, model, runs; only the first two have matching child nodes.

worked_examples.description: Check exact prefix arithmetic and honest rounding independently of labels; repaired _prefix_computation uses exact Operand values and Computation.build_equation.
Verify new emitted output from the selected tree; repaired _beat_8_commit replaces proposal slots and _adopt_ribbon_slot keeps group membership synchronized.

beats.purpose: Show a target-first-token miss on the modal draft.
beats.question: What goes wrong with one draft path?

narration.text: DFlash gave us three marginals from one parallel pass. Taking the argmax at each position yields 'the', 'model', 'works'. But the target model picks 'a' at the very first position, so the entire speculative path fails. That thirty-five percent mass for 'a' is wasted.

beats.purpose: Qualify the Q-based surrogate, then keep runner-up a ahead of deeper the-model.
beats.question: Why not keep the runner-up?

narration.text: Instead of betting on one path, DDTree keeps alternatives. For sequences drawn from the factorized draft distribution Q, expected matched depth is the sum of selected prefix masses. This is a draft-model proxy, not a target acceptance guarantee. A max-heap seeded with the best depth-one token selects the highest-mass prefixes. First pop: 'the' at point five five. Second pop: 'a' at point three five. Breadth beats the deeper candidate the-model at point three three.

beats.purpose: Multiply parent mass by a marginal.
beats.question: How are deeper masses computed?

narration.text: Third pop: the-model. Its mass is the parent's mass times the marginal. Point five five times point six zero equals point three three zero. The product means deeper nodes can never outrank their parent.

beats.purpose: Extend the second branch without recomputing a conditional marginal.
beats.question: Does the 'a' branch get deeper too?

narration.text: Fourth pop: a-model at point two one zero. Point three five times point six zero. Both major branches now extend to depth two.

Fifth: the-model-works, point three three zero times point five two, about point one seven two. Sixth: the-system at point one six five. Seventh: a-model-works at point one zero nine. Seven pops fill the budget. These are the seven highest-mass prefixes under the factorized draft distribution.

beats.purpose: Move nodes in insertion order while keeping positions based on depth.
beats.question: How does the target model see this tree?

narration.text: The target receives a flat array in insertion order: root, then best-first pops. The same nodes move; position IDs still come from tree depth. Both 'the' and 'a' use position one because they are alternatives at the same depth.

beats.purpose: Ancestry rather than array adjacency determines visibility.
beats.question: How does the target know which nodes are related?

narration.text: Tree attention restores the structure. Each node may attend to the committed context, its ancestors, and itself, but never to a sibling branch. Node 'the-model-works' sees root, 'the', 'the-model', and itself. One target forward pass computes the correct continuation for every prefix in parallel.

beats.purpose: Walk target choices until the missing runs child.
beats.question: Which path does the target choose?

narration.text: Verification walks the tree using the target's own decoding rule. At the root it picks 'a'. At 'a' it picks 'model'. At 'a-model' it picks 'runs', but that child is not in our tree, so the walk stops. The drafter's scores never chose this path; the target did.

beats.purpose: Matched nodes join output, followed by emitted next anchor runs.
beats.question: What gets committed?

narration.text: The matched tokens 'a' and 'model' join the committed context. 'Runs' becomes the next bonus token, ready for the following DFlash pass. Two speculative tokens were accepted instead of zero. Speed comes from proposals. Correctness still comes from the target.

transfer_questions.question: Can the product 0.33 times 0.52 be labeled exactly equal to 0.172?
transfer_questions.expected_answer: No. The exact value is 0.1716; 0.172 requires an approximation sign or explicit rounding label.
transfer_questions.justification: 33 times 52 is 1716 and the factors together have four decimal places. Rounded three-decimal display changes the number; a transform must not falsely assert equality.

transfer_questions.question: If a renderer commits only a and model and discards runs because it is absent from the tree, is its new output correct?
transfer_questions.expected_answer: No. It drops a target-selected token. The new output is a, model, runs, with runs anchoring the next round.
transfer_questions.justification: The walk's unmatched next_token is independently returned and appended after the matched tokens. Tree membership decides cached reuse, not whether to emit a target token.
